micro1 Agentic Workflows Hackathon · Solution demo

SelfHeal RAG

A company-policy RAG pipeline that catches its own stale answers and fixes them live — five minutes, six unedited command runs, one frozen 16-case test. Nothing below is staged.

1280×720 · 5:04 · captioned, no voiceover recorded from video/beats.html, real command output only

What's in the five minutes

0:00
Cold open — the corpus says $200, a ticket says $250. The handbook never got the memo.
0:30
Two strong baselines fail on camera — full-context (A0) and an unrestricted agent (B) both answer $200.
1:15
One genuine SelfHeal run — live self-heal fires, memory.json gains an entry, answer comes back $250, cited "MEMORY".
2:45
The verifier catches a stale citation — independent of memory, on the corpus's own document-revision history.
3:45
Frozen-test comparison — every baseline 0/3 on memory_correction, SelfHeal 3/3, confirmed by a direct ablation.
4:30
Hot take — the first official run scored 0/3, silently. What that bug was, and why the split itself is what caught it.
0/3→3/3
memory_correction accuracy on the frozen 16-case test — every baseline (full-context, static RAG, self-correcting RAG, unrestricted agent) scores zero; SelfHeal RAG scores 3/3, reproduced by a one-flag memory on/off ablation.
